hypothesis: A paired guest return-box and host member-projection can preserve the complete source test when the issue explicitly requires callable returned composites. A separate scalar-carrier probe rejects unsupported representation adapters before any defect claim.
input_policy: Original repository tests, their exact frontend source bytes and public issue text only. The historical cohort supplies the17-trial list and original source paths, not old candidate programs or labels.
design: Learn factory names, invocation methods, host container types, field selectors and member keys from source; use no task, repository or witness-ID branches.
checks: one top-level factory, one owned return, no self-name use
byte-exact clone except fresh factory name and boxing returned closure
lookup owner traces to the same guest program
one local result binding and all result uses receive the inverse projection
source host view and its imports match exact donor source
all complete source-test expected expressions remain unchanged
selection: Source retrieval rank, path, position, container kind, member and exact program hash; first16 per trial.
execution: Run scalar-carrier probe. A failed or unavailable probe never emits an alert. Run a candidate only after the probe passes with all controls and exact transport. Stop at first controlled candidate failure even if its independent repeat does not confirm.
limitations: The static checker covers a bounded Go-like guest grammar, not arbitrary language semantics.
A passing scalar probe establishes the container adapter, not the correctness of a returned closure.
Opaque effects and additional guest globals require full-test audit.
Applicability depends on an explicit public callable-composite contract.
This is development evidence; it does not establish generalization to independent tasks.
